summary: Full E2E test of BEATCUT MVP. Backend: 16/17 pytest tests pass (1 test bug fixed; 1 environment-related failure for brute-force lockout when going through public ingress with rotating proxy IPs — works perfectly via localhost). Frontend: landing/login/dashboard/Stripe checkout redirect/force-PRO/unsubscribe with AlertDialog/resubscribe button/studio iframe/logout all PASS. Demo user subscription reset to null at the end.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout uses `f"{request.client.host}:{email}"` as identifier. Behind the Kubernetes ingress/reverse-proxy the immediate request.client.host can rotate between pods/proxy IPs, so 5 failed attempts from a real attacker may not reliably trigger 429. Test confirmed: works correctly via localhost (lockout on 6th attempt), but fails via public URL (got 6x 401, no 429). Recommend using only email as identifier OR reading X-Forwarded-For real client IP.

issues: After clicking the nav logout button user lands on /login instead of the landing page /. Functionally fine (session cleared, protected routes blocked) but main-agent spec said 'redirect to landing'. Minor UX deviation.

action_items: (Optional, minor) Harden brute-force lockout for production behind a proxy: include X-Forwarded-For or rate-limit by email only.
(Optional, minor) Decide whether logout should redirect to / (landing) or /login — currently /login.

MongoDB _id properly excluded everywhere with projections {_id:0}.
JWT cookie set httponly+secure+samesite=lax — good. Google session cookie uses samesite=none+secure which is correct for cross-site OAuth flows.
seed_user idempotent and updates password if changed — good.
Server-side enforced PRO_PRICE (9.99 EUR) — payment amount cannot be tampered from frontend. Good.
Minor: brute-force identifier includes request.client.host — behind k8s ingress this rotates and weakens protection (see backend_issues.minor).

rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout test failure RCA: identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}' in /app/backend/server.py line ~262. When tests hit the public URL https://pro-mailer-2.preview.emergentagent.com, Kubernetes ingress/proxy forwards from rotating internal IPs, so login_attempts rows accumulate under different identifiers and the per-identifier count never reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS=5. Direct curl on localhost:8001 shows correct 401×5 then 429 (verified). Mitigation: read real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first hop) or simply key the rate-limit by email only for app-layer protection.
